newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Rival Cambodian troops clash near Phnom Penh.
newsitem.headline: Rival Cambodian troops clash near Phnom Penh.

text.p: Rival Cambodian government troops clashed on the outskirts of Phnom Penh on Saturday as troops loyal to Second Prime Minister Hun Sen moved in to search their rivals' military facilities.
A military official loyal to First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh said the clash was under way near a military base about 12 km (8 miles) northwest of the city.
"The fighting is starting now. CPP troops have come to our base," said the military official, who was inside the base, referring to troops loyal to Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party (CPP).
Witnesses in the area also reported hearing shooting but there were no reports of casualties.
The clash came as radio controlled by the CPP broadcast a warning from defence and security officials that searches were under way for "illegal troops" and weapons in the city.
Hun Sen warned earlier this week that Ranariddh's soldiers were bringing Khmer Rouge guerrilla defectors into the city illegally. Ranariddh has denied moving troops into the city.
